rationale: Split: test_size=0.25 gives the required quarter hold-out via a plain seeded random split; the target is defined afterwards, so no stratification. Target: paid_amount > 95th percentile with threshold_source=train_only, overriding the catalogue default of all_data, which would let test rows shape the threshold; the component reports threshold_value and per-partition positive rates and writes threshold.json. Features: only fields known at claim submission (claim type, CPT category, place of service, provider specialty, network status, service units, length of stay, ER/elective/preventive/auth flags, primary diagnosis, DRG presence). All five amount columns (billed, allowed, paid, member_oop, cob) are excluded because the label is derived from paid_amount and they are adjudication outputs; high_cost_flag is the dataset's own label proxy; claim_id and member_id are identifiers. Preprocessing: fit_on=train_only (overriding the leaky all_data default) so encoder and scaler never see test rows; standard scaling helps logistic regression converge on the count-valued numerics and is neutral for trees. Models: logistic_regression plus gradient_boosting as the single tree-based comparator; the component reports PR-AUC, ROC-AUC and precision/recall in the top 5 percent of test rows by score and writes model_metrics.json and precision_at_k.png. Report: caveats cover synthetic data, baseline-model limitations and no operational use as the task requires, plus class_imbalance because a 95th-percentile target has roughly 5 percent prevalence, which is why PR-AUC and top-k metrics matter more than ROC-AUC; show_denominators=true so positive rates and top-5-percent precision/recall print as counts over denominators; cite_artifacts=true so every reported number traces to threshold.json, feature_list.json or model_metrics.json. Feature and threshold artifacts are saved by their components.
